forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Knesset legal adviser officially recommended July 17 as dissolution date — two days AFTER the July 15 horizon. Knesset Speaker Ohana and coalition whip Katz have both aligned to the July 17 timetable. No second or third readings of the dissolution bill are scheduled before July 15. The Central Elections Committee (gov.il) confirmed the election date as October 27 — the statutory latest — satisfying neither the sub-Oct-27 nor the final-reading-by-July-15 criterion. Residual p=0.10 covers tail probability of a surprise accelerated vote.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will the US unilaterally announce a halt or formal pause of offensive strikes on Iranian territory before EOD 2026-07-11?
forecasts.delta_reason: Trump declared the MOU 'over' July 8 but simultaneously stated he does not expect all-out war and that any further operations would 'be over very quickly.' Pakistani PM Sharif attended Khamenei's burial in Mashhad today (July 9) and Pakistan stated readiness to immediately re-facilitate dialogue — creating a diplomatic opening as the funeral period closes. Iran's diplomacy was explicitly on hold for the funeral; resumption could enable US to pause strikes without losing face. Historical pattern in this conflict: both sides have de-escalated within 24-48h after short exchanges. Counter-weight: IRGC struck Kuwait and Bahrain bases July 8; Trump rhetoric at NATO summit is maximally aggressive.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if CENTCOM, the White House, or SecDef issues a public statement that the US has ceased or paused offensive strike operations against Iranian territory for at least 24 consecutive hours, before EOD 2026-07-11. A temporary hold for diplomatic purposes qualifies. Does NOT count: pauses due to weather or operational tempo only; silence without explicit announcement.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 only: CENTCOM press releases, White House official statements, Pentagon press briefings. Wire services (Reuters/AP/AFP) quoting named US officials qualify.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If strikes continue at reduced tempo without an official pause announcement, resolve NO. If US announces an 'operational pause' but explicitly reserves the right to strike immediately, resolve YES.

indicators.expected_effect: Pakistan PM Sharif in Mashhad today; any post-burial outreach to US by Pakistan within 24h would increase pause probability +10-15pp toward YES

indicators.expected_effect: If IRGC halts ship attacks post-funeral, US may pause retaliatory cycle; +10pp toward YES

forecasts.question: Will Iran's IRGC or affiliated forces conduct at least one additional confirmed attack on a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz or adjacent Gulf waters before EOD 2026-07-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: Iran's IRGC struck three commercial tankers on July 6-7 (Qatari LNG carrier al-Rakiyat, Saudi crude carrier Wedyan, a third vessel off Oman) while Khamenei's funeral procession departed Tehran. Iran has established a pattern of selective interdiction targeting vessels using the Omani-coast route without IRGC clearance. The MOU collapse removes the political constraint on further attacks. Counter-weight: Khamenei's burial concludes today (July 9); Pezeshkian government may reassert control over IRGC if diplomacy restarts post-funeral.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if at least one TIER1 source (Reuters, AP, AFP, CENTCOM, UK MARITIME TRADE OPERATIONS) reports a confirmed attack — missiles, drones, mines, or limpet mines — on a commercial vessel attributable to Iran, in the Strait of Hormuz or adjacent Gulf waters (Gulf of Oman, Persian Gulf), between 2026-07-10 and 2026-07-16 inclusive.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM, UK Maritime Trade Operations, or US Navy 5th Fleet statements are primary. Wire services quoting named military officials qualify. Shipping industry reports (Lloyd's, Dryad) qualify if corroborated by one government source.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If a vessel is damaged but attribution to Iran is not confirmed by at least one TIER1 source within 72h, resolve AMBIGUOUS. Houthi attacks in the Red Sea do NOT count — must be in Hormuz, Gulf of Oman, or Persian Gulf.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran agree to a new bilateral ceasefire, mutual pause, or structured negotiating framework (verified by both governments) before EOD 2026-07-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: The June 17 Islamabad MOU collapsed on July 7-8 after IRGC commercial ship attacks and US retaliatory strikes. However: Pakistan PM Sharif is in Mashhad today and stated Pakistan 'ready to keep facilitating dialogue'; Iranian diplomacy was explicitly on hold for the funeral, which ends today; Trump left the door open ('not sure' about wanting a deal, implying not definitively closed); oil prices rose 5% on Trump's 'deal is over' statement creating economic pressure; and this conflict has seen multiple rapid de-escalation cycles including three ceasefires since February. The 13-day window is sufficient for a diplomatic turnaround if both sides want one.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if both the US (White House or CENTCOM) AND Iran (Iranian MFA or presidency) publicly confirm a new ceasefire, mutual cessation of strikes, or a structured negotiating framework agreed between the two governments, before EOD 2026-07-22. Must be bilateral — a unilateral US pause alone does NOT qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters, AP, AFP, Al Jazeera reporting both sides confirming. Official statements from both governments mandatory. A mediator (Pakistan/Qatar) announcement with explicit confirmation from both sides counts.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If one side announces a ceasefire but the other has not confirmed within 24h, resolve AMBIGUOUS. If talks resume but no ceasefire or framework is announced (only 'talks underway'), resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will the UK/France-led multinational mine-countermeasure (MCM) mission begin active mine-clearing operations in the Strait of Hormuz before EOD 2026-08-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: As of July 6, The National reported UK/France finalizing Hormuz MCM mission 'within days,' with logistics hub at Oman's Port of Duqm confirmed and 10+ NATO members contributing; Britain's RFA Lyme Bay designated MCM mother ship. However: resumption of US-Iran hostilities July 7-8 created an unsafe operating environment; Iran explicitly warned Britain and France against deploying; EU Aviation Safety Agency extended no-fly warnings over Iran through August 31. The 37-day window to August 15 is sufficient time for a new ceasefire (F10) to enable launch, but operational safety risk remains if hostilities continue.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source (Royal Navy, French Navy, EUNAVFOR, or equivalent national defense ministry) confirms that MCM vessels or operations have ACTIVELY commenced clearing mines in the Strait of Hormuz — not merely deployed to the region — before EOD 2026-08-15. Deployment to Port of Duqm staging area alone does NOT qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Royal Navy or French Navy official statements. UK MoD or French Defense Ministry press releases. CENTCOM confirmation of coalition MCM operations. Corroborated wire service reports citing named military officials.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If MCM vessels are in the Hormuz region but Iran launches attacks on them before clearing operations begin, resolve AMBIGUOUS. If operations begin and are then suspended within 24h due to hostilities, resolve YES (operations DID commence).

indicators.name: New US-Iran ceasefire enabling safe MCM operating environment
indicators.expected_effect: A ceasefire before July 22 (F10) is the primary enabling condition for MCM mission launch; +20-25pp toward YES if F10 resolves YES

forecasts.question: Will Iran's IRGC conduct a confirmed missile or drone strike on a military or critical infrastructure target in Saudi Arabia or the UAE before EOD 2026-08-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Iran's IRGC struck US military installations in Kuwait (Camp Arifjan, Ali Al Salem) and Bahrain (Shaikh Isa, Juffair) on July 8 in retaliation for US strikes. Saudi Arabia and UAE host US forces (Prince Sultan Air Base, Al Dhafra Air Base) but have maintained studied neutrality; Iran has historically avoided direct attacks on Saudi/Emirati targets to preserve economic relationships. IRGC expanding strikes to Saudi/UAE territory would be a significant escalatory step. Risk is elevated given the IRGC's demonstrated willingness to strike Kuwait/Bahrain on July 8, but Saudi/UAE are a different political calculation.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source (CENTCOM, Saudi MoD, UAE MoD, or Reuters/AP/AFP citing named officials) confirms an IRGC-attributed missile or drone strike that caused physical damage to a military installation or critical infrastructure on Saudi Arabian or UAE territory, before EOD 2026-08-15. Houthi attacks from Yemen do NOT count — must be directly IRGC-conducted.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM or named Saudi/UAE military official confirmation mandatory. Wire service corroboration with explicit IRGC attribution required.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If an attack occurs and Saudi/UAE deny or attribute to a non-Iranian actor, resolve AMBIGUOUS pending further investigation. If intercepted before impact with no physical damage, resolve NO.

indicators.expected_effect: Formal diplomatic break increases IRGC targeting rationale +10pp toward YES

forecasts.question: Will the Iranian government formally notify the IAEA of its withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty before 2027-01-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: FDD (March 30) documented Iran officially reviving NPT withdrawal threats; NCRI reported Majlis members discussing 'imported warheads' and NPT exit following IAEA board resolutions. FM Araghchi framed enrichment as 'national pride.' However: US and Israeli strikes on Natanz and Fordow destroyed or severely degraded enrichment infrastructure (Arms Control Association confirmed), making NPT withdrawal carry no practical nuclear benefit while the program is disabled. Pezeshkian has consistently avoided formal withdrawal as a diplomatic card. China, India, and Pakistan — whose ambassadors attended today's burial — would face catastrophic pressure if Iran withdrew, making it very high-cost for minimal operational gain.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran's foreign ministry or presidency formally notifies the IAEA Director General of intent to withdraw from the NPT, OR if Iran's Majlis passes a binding resolution mandating NPT withdrawal, before 2027-01-01. Rhetorical threats from MPs, IRGC officials, or IRNA commentators do NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA official communication only for DG notification. Majlis vote confirmed by at least two TIER1 sources (Reuters, AP, BBC, Al Jazeera) citing named legislative officials.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Iran 'suspends' NPT obligations without a formal withdrawal notification, resolve NO — suspension is not withdrawal. If the IAEA confirms receipt of a withdrawal notification, resolve YES regardless of subsequent Iranian government statements.
